messages.subject: Question
messages.body: diffgate worker, plan amendment needs one ruling on HOW the owner rule 'reviewer and reviser sessions never run the writing script' works. The S1 briefs let the reviewer write only its report and the reviser only the spec plus its disposition file, so the ledger steps (begin before each review, check after each review, fixcheck after each fix) become coordinator-inserted step tasks with their own brief templates. Open point: the SPEC gives the reviewer one in-session repair turn when check rejects its findings block, and has the reviser write and validate <DIR>/fixmap-r<N>.txt itself. My recommended design (A): the reviewer and reviser sessions may run only READ-ONLY script calls that write nothing (status, check --dry-run, fixcheck --dry-run) to self-validate; the reviser writes its fix map as a '## Diffgate fixmap' block inside its own disposition file (its allowed output); the coordinator's inserted steps run begin, check (and append the script's closing block and verdict line to the report), and fixcheck --map <disposition file>. Alternative (B), strict: the sessions never invoke diffgate.py at all; a rejected findings block gets no repair turn (the check step resubmits once, so anchor errors degrade to deferred: unanchored), and an unmapped fix hunk is sent back to a re-dispatched reviser task. Which?
